entities.text: WHO Nutrient and Promotion Profile Model
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

nary_nodes.label: Analysis of toddler foods
evidence: research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves
To do the research, Hudson and her team photographed foods marketed to children between 6 and 36 months at 21 grocery stores in Austin, Texas.
Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed, according to research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves.

nary_nodes.label: Presentation of research findings
evidence: presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition

nary_nodes.label: 80% of toddler foods ultraprocessed
evidence: Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed
The answer is over 80% of the products are ultraprocessed

nary_nodes.label: Nearly half fail nutrition standards
evidence: Nearly half of those items also failed to meet at least one nutritional benchmark for children set by the World Health Organization.

nary_nodes.label: Sugar-failing products four times more likely ultraprocessed
evidence: We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed

nary_nodes.label: Quarter of foods high in sodium
evidence: Almost a quarter of the foods were higher in sodium than is recommended

nary_nodes.label: 71% of baby foods contain additives
evidence: over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives
What shocked me was the top ingredient in 71% of these baby foods wasn’t a fruit or vegetable — it was one or more additives
Prior research published in January found over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives

nary_nodes.label: Parents cannot tell ultraprocessed from aisle
evidence: parents really cannot tell that from just walking down the aisle

nary_nodes.label: Ultraprocessed foods crowd out healthy foods
evidence: The problem isn’t just what’s in these high-sugar, high-salt ultraprocessed foods, it’s what they crowd out

nary_nodes.label: Toddlers can eat family foods
evidence: Kids can eat whatever healthy foods and snacks the family is eating — just chop or mash it up

evidence: America’s trusted household brands offer parents and caregivers a wide variety of safe, affordable and convenient product choices

evidence: parents should prepare healthy foods at home instead of using store-bought foods

evidence: Parents shouldn’t have to decode every package in the grocery store to find healthy food for toddlers
